references.text: God promises Abraham descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, continuing the promise of a great offspring.
The angel promises Hagar that her descendants will be so numerous they cannot be counted, similar to the promise given to Abraham.
The promise concerning Abraham's descendants is repeated with a comparison to the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.
The promise to Abraham is reiterated to Isaac, emphasizing a multitude of descendants.
God repeats the promise to Jacob, Abraham's grandson, about descendants as numerous as the dust of the earth—the same imagery found in Genesis 13:16.
Jacob reminds God of the promise to make his descendants as numerous as the sand by the sea.
Balaam asks, 'Who can count the dust of Jacob?'—a direct allusion to the promise in Genesis 13:16 using the same dust metaphor.
The book of Hebrews points to the fulfillment of the promise regarding Abraham's numerous descendants, compared to the stars and the sand.
The original covenant formulation underlying the promise of numerous descendants.
Prophetic fulfillment of the covenant promise to make the people numerous once again.
The original wording of the promise to make Abraham into a great nation.
A prophetic allusion to Abraham's promise, contrasted with the people's disobedience.
Prophetic confirmation of the promise to make the people numerous once more.
Prophetic renewal of the promise to make the people many and honorable.
Retelling of the covenant promise to Jacob, affirming both multitude and land.
Clear theological contrast: 'dust' as curse and destruction versus the promise of life.
Part of the same covenant promise, confirming that Sarah will also become a nation.
Central covenant formulation concerning fertility and becoming a nation.
Retelling of the promise with 'sand' as a metaphor, affirming continuity.
The central covenant formulation serving as the basis for the promise of descendants.
